issues.legal_issue: An executing court cannot entertain an application to set aside an execution sale when it is filed after the prescribed limitation period and no applicable provision authorizes an extension.
material_facts: The execution sale took place on 25 May 1981.
The judgment-debtor’s objections to the sale were dismissed on 4 May 1982.
The judgment-debtor filed an application to set aside the sale on 28 May 1982, more than sixty days after the sale.
The executing court nevertheless allowed the judgment-debtor time to make deposits, but the period for filing the application had not been fixed by the court.
The High Court set aside the executing court’s order because the application was time-barred.
issues.conclusion: The executing court had no jurisdiction to entertain the application filed after the limitation period; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 127 of the Limitation Act prescribes sixty days from the date of sale for an application to set aside a sale in execution. Section 5 of that Act expressly excludes applications under Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, so it cannot extend the period for an application under Order XXI Rule 89. Section 148 of the Code does not apply where the court did not fix the time for making the application. The executing court therefore cannot entertain an application under Order XXI Rule 89 after the Article 127 period has expired.

rule.if: execution_sale_set_aside_application and filed_after_prescribed_period and made_under_execution_procedure and filing_period_not_fixed_by_court

predicates.execution_sale_set_aside_application: A party applied to set aside a sale conducted through execution of a decree.
predicates.filed_after_prescribed_period: The applicant filed the application after the applicable limitation period had expired.
predicates.made_under_execution_procedure: The application was made under the procedure governing execution of decrees.
predicates.filing_period_not_fixed_by_court: The court had not fixed the period for making the application.

issues.definition: When an application to set aside an execution sale is made under execution procedure after the prescribed period, and the court did not fix the filing period, the executing court lacks jurisdiction to entertain it.

issues.legal_issue: The concurrent rejection of objections to an execution sale did not warrant interference on special leave.
material_facts: The executing court dismissed the judgment-debtors’ objections to the sale.
The High Court affirmed that dismissal.
The judgment-debtors challenged the High Court’s order by special leave petition.
issues.conclusion: The Court found no reason to interfere with the High Court’s order and dismissed the special leave petition.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that it found no reason to interfere with the High Court’s order affirming the dismissal of the objections; it gave no further legal reasoning or test for that conclusion.

predicates.special_leave_challenge_to_sale_objectio: A party brought a special leave challenge to the rejection of objections to an execution sale.
predicates.objections_rejected_by_lower_courts: The executing court rejected the objections and the High Court affirmed that rejection.

issues.definition: When a special leave challenge concerns objections to an execution sale rejected by the lower courts, the challenge is dismissed without interference where the Court finds no reason to interfere.
